news.title: Woman’s High Court case against adult websites adjourned over $120m US settlement
news.text:
A High Court case in which a woman claims recordings of her being sexually abused as child appeared on adult websites associated with Pornhub has been adjourned for six months after a judge was told that approval is awaited of a $120 million (€107 million) settlement of an associated class action in the United States.

The woman, who lives in the US and has been given the name “Jane Doe” to protect her identity, claims she was drugged and raped by a man when she was a minor.

She claims her abuser recorded what happened and posted the images online.

It is alleged that videos of her abuse were published and distributed on adult video-sharing websites owned by the group of companies that own, control and manage internet pornography websites including Pornhub.

As a result, a class action on behalf of the woman and others has been brought in the US courts against various parties within the MindGeek (now renamed AYLO) group of companies. MindGeek, before its name change, is Pornhub’s parent. 

The woman’s allegations of wrongdoing by the group have been denied.

In a damages claim before the US courts, the woman alleges she has been victimised and has been exploited by the defendants for profit.

Due to the international structure of the defendant group, the woman sought to bring parallel proceedings before the Irish courts. It is also alleged that the Irish entities have substantial assets.

The defendants in the Irish action include the limited companies AYLO Billing, Mirmay, Nutaku Publishing, Appatomic and Liquidum, which all have a registered address at The Black Church, St Mary’s Place, Dublin. 

Other defendants in her proceedings also include MG Freesites Ltd, MG Freesites II Ltd, AYLO Premium Ltd, MG Social Ltd, MindGeek USA Incorporated and MindGeek SARL, which is registered in Luxembourg.

In her Irish proceeding the woman seeks orders including aggravated and exemplary damages for what she claims is the defendants breach of duty and for breaches of GDPR, conspiracy and her right to privacy.

She also wants an order directing the defendants to identify and remove images of child sexual abuse from the websites and the identities of users who have uploaded the images.

The woman also wants an order directing the defendants to preserve all assets and cash reserves in Ireland below an amount of $630 million pending the outcome of the actions in Ireland and the US.

In the US, the defendants recently agreed to settle a class action, on behalf of the woman and others depicted in the material, and pay $120 million. 

MindGeek also agreed to injunctive relief which will see it make substantial changes to its sites in order to protect children. The settlement is subject to court approval in the US.

The Irish case was back before the High Court on Wednesday when barrister Robert O’Reilly, for the woman, sought an adjournment to allow for the approval of a $120 million settlement of the US proceedings in Alabama. 

Judge Brian Cregan adjourned the case to March.
news.summary: ‘Jane Doe’ says recordings of her being abused as a minor were published on video-sharing sites

news.title: RTÉ rejects minister’s claim reforms have been slow as €20m funding cut confirmed
news.text:
His comments came as the Government confirmed that RTÉ will receive €240m in 2027, €20m less than the broadcaster had been anticipating under its multi-annual funding agreement.

Mr O’Donovan said the €11m increase in funding for RTÉ accounted for a large part of his department’s additional funding for 2027. If RTÉ were given its full €260m allocation, he said, this would represent nearly 70% of his department’s budget uplift.

RTÉ is currently in the middle of a €725m three-year multi-annual agreement with the Government, but sources said there had been concerns about the pace of contingent reforms, a charge RTÉ has rejected.

Mr Bakhurst said the reduced funding would mean RTÉ “has important decisions to make”, given commitments already made to audiences, the independent sector, other stakeholders and staff.

“The Government's decision to reduce this public funding agreement by €20m at this late stage, when we have already made important commitments to our audiences, to the independent sector, to other important stakeholders and to RTÉ staff, is one we had not anticipated and will inevitably impact on our ability to deliver our five-year strategy.” 

RTÉ seeks meeting with minister 

Mr Bakhurst said RTÉ chair Terence O’Rourke was seeking a meeting with the minister regarding the multi-annual commitment made in 2024, “particularly given that RTÉ has committed to numerous agreements with its stakeholders based on this written and extensively publicised agreement”.

“In fact, the Taoiseach and the Tánaiste said at the time, that predictable multi-annual funding is key to RTÉ being able to deliver a strategy.” 

Mr Bakhurst said the clarity provided by the multi-annual funding agreement had enabled RTÉ to plan ahead, deliver trusted and independent news and analysis, produce more public service programmes and content, including original Irish drama and live sport, and invest in podcasts, apps and the RTÉ Player.

He also said the agreement had enabled RTÉ to implement a digital commercial strategy, stabilise its finances and progress its plans.
news.summary: Kevin Bakhurst said RTÉ had made commitments based on its multi-annual agreement and warned the funding reduction would affect its strategy
news.author: Irishexaminer.com,Paul Hosford
